title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graces the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences in Thiruvananthapuram
subtitle:
“Technology Can Assist a Doctor, But Cannot Replace the Human Aspects of a Doctor”: Vice-President urges medical graduates to combine scientific excellence with human compassion

Access to Higher Education is Central to the Vision of Viksit Bharat: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today attended the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences in Thiruvananthapuram, as the Chief Guest.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 15th Graduation Day Ceremony of Sree Uthradom Thirunal (SUT) Academy of Medical Sciences, Thiruvananthapuram today.
Governor of Keralam Shri Rajendra Viswanath Arlekar; Minister for Labour, Animal Husbandry and Women and Child…
pic.twitter.com/G4prIanwxm
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 27, 2026
Addressing the graduating students, the Vice-President highlighted the important place of SUT Academy of Medical Sciences in Keralam’s healthcare and medical education landscape.
“The true strength of a medical institute lies in the quality of education it provides, the doctors it produces, the research it undertakes and the patients it serves,” the Vice-President said.
Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said the graduating doctors are entering healthcare at an extraordinary time, when Artificial Intelligence, robotics, digital health, advanced imaging and precision medicine are transforming the sector.
In this context, he said, the inauguration of Robotic Surgery and Computer-Aided Diagnosis facilities at the Institute is significant and reflects the importance of keeping medical education and healthcare aligned with technological progress.
However, he stressed that technology must never displace the human dimension of medicine. “Technology can assist a doctor, but it cannot replace the human aspects of a doctor,” he said. “A machine can analyse. A robot can assist. An algorithm can identify patterns. But a patient still needs a doctor who can listen, understand, reassure and take responsibility,” he added.
The Vice-President urged the graduates to protect the trust represented by the white coat by being accurate in diagnosis, honest in communication, compassionate in treatment and ethical in every decision.He emphasised that scientific excellence and human compassion must always go together.
The Vice-President said Bharat is striding confidently towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.He said the Prime Minister has emphasised that Viksit Bharat can be achieved only when every State, district and village develops, and noted that access to higher education is at the core of this national vision.
Highlighting the expansion of medical education over the past twelve years, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said that while there was only one AIIMS in New Delhi earlier, 12 new AIIMS have been established.
The Vice-President said he has attended convocations across the length and breadth of Bharat and observed a welcome trend of more women receiving degrees and medals than men.
He noted that at the present graduation ceremony, 60 women and 32 men are receiving undergraduate degrees, while 5 women and 2 men doctors are receiving postgraduate degrees.He described this as a welcome development.
Giving three guiding principles to the graduating doctors, the Vice-President urged them to carry:Knowledge in their minds, Compassion in their hearts, Integrity in their conduct.
He asked the graduates to be confident while remaining humble, ambitious while remaining ethical, technologically advanced while remaining compassionate, and successful while remaining connected to society.He also urged the young doctors to “always say No to drugs.”
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan wished the graduates a successful, meaningful and fulfilling professional journey and said, “May you always remember that the greatest privilege of being a doctor is the opportunity to make a difference in another human being’s life.”He also wished SUT Academy of Medical Sciences continued growth as a centre of excellence in medical education, healthcare, research and innovation.
The ceremony was attended by Governor of Tamil Nadu and Keralam Shri Rajendra Viswanath Arlekar; Minister for Labour, Animal Husbandry and Women and Child Development, Government of Keralam, Smt. Bindhu Krishna; Chairman, SUT Academy of Medical Sciences, Dr. A. C. Shanmugam; Vice Chancellor, Kerala University of Health Sciences, Dr. Mohanan Kunnummal; faculty, staff, graduating students and their families.

title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan Participates in Vishwa Seva Dinam Celebrations Marking Mata Amritanandamayi Devi’s 73rd Birthday in Amritapuri , Kollam
subtitle:

Amma is a miracle, Her Life is a Message of Love, Compassion and Selfless Service: Vice-President

Humanity Needs Compassionate Advancement Alongside Technological Progress: Vice-President

True Greatness of Seva Lies in the Transformation of Human Lives: Vice-President

Viksit Bharat Will Be an Inclusive Bharat Where No One Is Left Behind: Vice-President

“Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi” Must Guide Bharat’s Journey Towards Viksit Bharat: Vice-President
date:

                27 SEP 2026 2:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:

The Vice-President also released the Amritakuteeram 30th Anniversary Souvenir, commemorating the completion of 50,000 homes across India and Sri Lanka, along with three new Ashram publications: The Hanuman Chalisa, The Ocean of Grace and Satyam Shivam Sundaram.

September 27, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President described it as a “profound privilege and a matter of immense happiness” to be present at Amritapuri on the occasion of Amma’s 73rd birthday. He offered his respectful pranam to Mata Amritanandamayi Devi and wished her a long life dedicated to the service of the nation.
Recalling an earlier occasion when he had invited Amma to a programme in Coimbatore, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said he still remembered the long stream of thousands of people who had gathered to greet her and seek her blessings.
Paying tribute to Amma’s lifelong service, the Vice-President said her life is a message of love, compassion and selfless service. He said her life reminds the nation of a timeless truth of Bharat, that Seva is a way of life and an expression of oneness with humanity.
He recalled that from childhood itself, Amma felt the suffering of people around her and responded with food, clothing, affection and compassion. At the heart of this service, he said, is the spiritual understanding that all beings share an essential divine oneness.
Highlighting healthcare as one of the most inspiring dimensions of the Mata Amritanandamayi Math’s humanitarian work, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said that, charitable medical care worth over ₹890 crore has been provided in Bharat since 1998, benefiting more than 64 lakh patients through free treatment and surgeries.
Recalling the inauguration of Amrita Hospital at Faridabad in August 2022, the Vice-President referred to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s description of Amma as an embodiment of “love, compassion, service and sacrifice” and as a carrier of India’s spiritual tradition.
The Vice-President said Seva is also about creating opportunities for the future.He noted that more than 55,000 scholarships have been provided worldwide by the Math and highlighted tablet-aided education, after-school tutoring, adult literacy and vocational training initiatives aimed at opening new pathways for disadvantaged communities.
He particularly highlighted the empowerment of women through AmritaSREE. He said around 2.5 lakh women from poor and vulnerable communities have been supported through start-up capital, vocational training and microfinance, with more than 15,000 Self-Help Groups.
“When a woman becomes economically empowered, the impact extends far beyond the individual,” he said, noting that it strengthens families and communities.
He said Nari Shakti is not simply about participation, but about empowerment, dignity, opportunity and leadership.
The Vice-President said what began with the compassion of a young girl in a village has grown into a humanitarian movement touching millions of lives in Bharat and across the world.
He highlighted the construction of more than 50,000 homes for the homeless, scholarships for thousands of children, pensions for more than one lakh impoverished people and livelihood initiatives.
While noting the impressive scale of the work, he said the real greatness lies in the human lives behind the numbers. Service, he added, must therefore be understood not merely through statistics but through the transformation it creates in human lives.
The Vice-President said the true test of Seva often comes during times of crisis and highlighted the Math’s humanitarian response to disasters and emergencies.
He referred to the organisation’s assistance during the Indian Ocean tsunami, Gujarat earthquake, Uttarakhand floods, Keralam floods, COVID-19 pandemic and Wayanad landslides.
He also highlighted the Math’s contribution of ₹100 crore to the Government of India’s Namami Gange programme, along with tree plantation, cleanliness drives and initiatives for sustainable rural living.
Referring to the Amala Bharatam initiative, he said it has undertaken large numbers of cleanliness drives across the country, while more than 10 lakh trees have been planted worldwide as part of the UN Billion Tree Campaign.
The Vice-President said the spirit inspiring Amma’s work is deeply connected to the civilisational ethos of Bharat.He said Seva has no boundaries of caste, creed, language, region or nationality and recognises only one identity-humanity. He described this as the underlying philosophy of Vishwa Seva Dinam.
Referring to the multiple challenges facing the world, including conflicts, humanitarian crises, natural disasters, displacement, poverty, loneliness and environmental challenges, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said humanity needs more than technological advancement. “It needs compassionate advancement,” he said.
The Vice-President said Bharat is progressing towards the vision of a Viksit Bharat, and development requires infrastructure, technology, investment, innovation and economic growth.However, he stressed that development must also have a human face.
“While marching towards attaining a Viksit Bharat, we must ensure that modernity and our civilisational values move together,” he said, adding that “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi” should be the guiding mantra.He also called for ensuring that Viksit Bharat is an inclusive Bharat where no one is left behind.
Concluding his address, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan offered his respectful pranam to Mata Amritanandamayi Devi and said that Amma is a miracle and should continue to guide us in serving society and the nation.He expressed the hope that the noble movement would continue to touch millions of lives and that Seva would become the foundation of a more peaceful, sustainable and compassionate world.
The programme was attended by Governor of Keralam and Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; Chief Minister of Keralam Shri V. D. Satheesan; Union Minister for Civil Aviation Shri Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu; Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Suresh Gopi; Speaker of the Keralam Legislative Assembly Shri Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan; Ministers of the Government of Keralam; Justice Gopinath of the Kerala High Court; MPs Shri NK Premachandran and Shri Shashi Tharoor, Ambassador of Nepal to India ,Shri Surender Thapa, MLAs, Swamijis, devotees and volunteers.

title: English rendering of PM’s address in the 138th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 27.09.2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 11:40AM by PIB Delhi
content:
My dear countrymen, Namaskar.
I am getting an opportunity to meet you once again for the September edition of ‘Mann Ki Baat’. I welcome all the people of the country. In ‘Mann Ki Baat’, we provide a platform for the positive efforts of our countrymen… discuss the nation's achievements. One such major, historic achievement of India is set to mark its 10th anniversary in just a day – this achievement is the ‘Surgical Strike’. Ten years ago, on September 28-29, 2016, the Indian Army carried out surgical strikes on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan. The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the Line of Control (LoC) to take action against terrorism.
The surgical strike boldly demonstrated to the entire world a new example of India’s counter-terrorism policy. The ‘Surgical Strike’ was our decisive response to the long-standing pain India had endured due to terrorist attacks. Over the past decade - from the Balakot airstrike to ‘Operation Sindoor’ - India has repeatedly sent a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast an evil eye on India, they will be met with a befitting response.
Friends,
India has long suffered wounds inflicted by terrorist attacks. There was a time when serial blasts had become a common occurrence in the country. It was in this very month of September - specifically on September 13, 2008 - that many innocent lives were lost in the serial blasts in Delhi. Just a few weeks later, the massive 26/11 attack took place in Mumbai. Friends, in the past too, there used to be demands for action against Pakistan following every terror attack, but such calls were often not given due attention; time to pass by was simply awaited. Today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and we are witnessing the results of that.
Friends,
This year also marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks. Among the innocent lives lost at the World Trade Center in the US, the highest number of victims—after Americans - was Indians. I recall that after becoming Prime Minister in 2014, when I visited the US, I had reached New York to pay my homage to those innocent citizens. Today, once again, I extend my condolences to the bereaved families on behalf of crores of Indian citizens.
My dear countrymen,
A grand picture of the nation is currently emerging. This picture includes you, your family and even your neighbours. I am referring to India's census. The first phase of this exercise is nearly complete across all states and union territories;
data of over 32 crore families has already been recorded. Work is currently underway also in the remote, snow-clad regions of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttarakhand. Many inspiring experiences have emerged from these areas. In Uttarakhand, the census process began in the village of Mana in Chamoli; Mana is known as the country's first village. The process there started with 83-year-old Purnima Rawat ji. In Bagori village, Uttarkashi, Hardev Singh Rana ji—who runs a homestay—entered his details himself using digital means.
Friends,
The census is a national responsibility for all of us. On 15th August also, I had urged my countrymen to take time out for that. The facility to self-register your census details is very convenient. You can register information about yourself and your family from your mobile itself. Along with Hindi, this facility is available in 16 languages.
Friends,
To do this, you need to visit the census online portal. The portal is se.census.gov.in… log in using your mobile number, enter your location, fill in the details regarding your family and submit the information. The entire process takes about 15 to 20 minutes. And for that you do not need to upload any document. After submitting the information, you will receive a special ID. You can share this ID with the census enumerator when they visit your home. After the information you provided is verified, it will become part of the census record.
Friends,
So far, more than 2 crore 60 lakh people have already entered their details on the census portal via mobile - completing the self-enumeration. It will take a little of your time, but it is important for the nation, as accurate information about you and your family helps create a precise picture of the country's future.
My dear countrymen,
Today - the date 27th of September - has become even more special for a special reason. Today marks the 100th birth anniversary of a great personality who had dedicated his entire life to culture, society, and the nation. I am speaking of the revered late Ashok Singhal ji, the former International Working President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad. He was born on this very day - September 27, 1926 - in Agra. Living amidst society, he led life like an ascetic. The very direction and energy he imparted to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement veritably resulted in us witnessing the magnificent temple in Ayodhya today. I’ve been greatly fortunate… I’ve not only observed his life closely but also have had the opportunity to join him in this mission. It was only natural for me to be reminded of Ashok ji repeatedly while participating in the Pran Pratishtha ceremony at the Ram Mandir.
Friends,
There are so many aspects about Ashok ji that do not receive much attention. Alongside the Ram Mandir movement, he also waged a major battle against social discrimination and inequality. He was born into a very affluent family; his father was a civil services official, and most of his siblings held high-ranking positions. He himself was a graduate of IIT BHU. Yet, despite all that, he dedicated his life to society and culture - this is the hallmark of great individuals. Today, on the occasion of his birth centenary, I bow to him on behalf of his millions of admirers… I offer my heartfelt tribute, on my part.
My dear countrymen,
We began this year with a grand celebration of national pride – This festival was the "Somnath Swabhiman Parv". A thousand years ago, in 1026, Mahmud of Ghazni had demolished the Somnath Temple for the first time. However, those who came to destroy Somnath and erase India's identity have no existence at all today, whereas the Somnath Temple stands in all its grandeur by the vast sea, bestowing the blessing of immortality upon India. That is why we celebrated the 'Somnath Swabhiman Parv' this year with immense pride.
Friends,
Why I am bringing this up again in 'Mann Ki Baat' today - there is a special reason for that. In 1026 AD when Somnath was destroyed by Ghazni; the same year, the famous Sun Temple in Modhera, Gujarat, was also attacked and destroyed. This means that a thousand years have passed since the destruction of the Modhera temple as well, whereas the temple then had been built just a year ago. King Bhimdev had got it built in 1025.
Friends,
Imagine that era; a massive invasion had taken place, a major center of faith like the Somnath Temple had been vandalised, and attacks were occurring at multiple locations - any society or administration could have had its morale shattered. Yet, King Bhimdev The First not only confronted the forces of Ghazni but also had the Modhera Sun Temple rebuilt within a short time. It is because of this very resilience that the Somnath Temple, too, was rebuilt every time despite facing repeated destruction.
Friends,
The attacks on the Modhera Sun Temple did not cease in later periods either. Alauddin Khilji later destroyed this temple, the magnificent architectural marvel once again. However, friends, we, the people of India, do not worship the Sun solely through architecture and temples; for us, Sun worship also signifies light, energy, science, and the inspiration for continuity. That is why Modhera is known today not just for its Sun Temple; this village in Gujarat has become the country's first ‘Surya Gram’ 'Solar Village.'
Modhera now runs entirely on solar energy, setting an example of sustainability for the nation. Several attractions and amenities for tourists have also been introduced in Modhera. The Modhera Dance Festival is held there in January, following Makar Sankranti, featuring magnificent performances of India's cultural and classical dances. I would urge all of you to visit Modhera at least once and witness this glorious Indian heritage.
Friends,
Our connection with the past remains very much alive today. This is driven by the dedication and hard work of individuals who are deepening this bond. A unique initiative of this kind is underway in Manapparai, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu. A. Selvaraju ji, associated with the Department of Tamil Studies at a college, is spearheading this effort. During a lecture, he learned about some ancient sculptures from a student. Following a discussion on the subject, he planned a field visit. During this visit, he discovered several sculptures and ancient temples at various locations. This is a fascinating way to connect with the past; this way, we can understand our heritage even better. Similar initiatives can be undertaken in other parts of the country as well… they offer us the opportunity to observe and comprehend our history more closely.
My dear countrymen,
In just a few days, it’s the 2nd of October - the birth anniversary of revered Bapu. Bapu has given us many guiding principles for life… cleanliness is one of them. We often see numerous efforts related to cleanliness around us. These efforts are very inspiring and uplifting. Such photos, videos, and reels frequently catch our attention on social media as well. I have witnessed many such initiatives recently. At a place in Madhya Pradesh, young people are working to clean up a river; the entire community is joining in their small effort. Similarly, in Andhra Pradesh, the youth are cleaning up old stepwells and wells, thereby helping to restore our ancient heritage. In Mumbai, some young people are taking the initiative to keep beaches clean; every week, hundreds of young friends gather at one beach or the other to serve through cleanliness drives... Swachhata Se Sewa. Here in Delhi, children and the youth are raising awareness about segregating waste and maintaining cleanliness in their surroundings. In West Bengal, young students are collaborating with locals to clean up market areas at picnic spots.
Friends,
Across all these efforts, one aspect is easily observed… somewhere it starts with a single individual, other people join in, and the movement grows - this is precisely what 'Jan-Bhagidari' is all about. Indeed, cleanliness is the most beautiful tribute we can pay to Bapu.
My dear countrymen,
When we protect the environment, we do not merely save plants or animals; we strengthen that entire ecosystem. Some initiatives taking place in various parts of the country are beautifully highlighting this sentiment.
Friends,
There is the Sonai Rupai Wildlife Sanctuary in Assam. There was a time when elephants used to inhabit this area, but as human interference on forest land increased, the elephants moved away. Three years ago, this land was cleared of encroachment, and the results have been remarkable - the elephants have returned here again. Herds of elephants are once again being spotted in areas where they had not been active for years. Friends, another wonderful initiative has taken place in Assam itself - this effort is to save a tiny creature, the Pygmy Hog. Once, its very existence was under threat; at that time, a conservation program was launched with just six Pygmy Hogs, and they were reintroduced into the wild. Grasslands were also curated for their living. Today, thanks to this program, the Pygmy Hog population has risen to over 190.
Friends,
Our relationship with nature is not limited merely to its preservation; often, when we care for nature, it becomes a source of sustenance for our own lives. In the Sundarbans of West Bengal, some women are setting an inspiring example of this very bond. These women from Jharkhali are creating mangrove forests.
Most of them are women who lost their husbands to tiger attacks. After losing their husbands, they found a means of livelihood within the Sundarbans itself. The mangroves they have planted are now serving as a natural protective shield for their villages, while also providing them with an income. Friends, let us conserve the environment, respect the balance of nature, and safeguard its diversity. Every such effort of ours is a responsibility we owe to future generations.
My dear countrymen,
Millions of young people across the country have recently taken a significant resolve against substance abuse and drugs. They have vowed to stay away from drugs themselves and have also taken up the responsibility of spreading this message to others - all under the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan'. This campaign will run for 100 weeks… it includes volunteers from 'MY Bharat'. Our youth associated with the NSS are part of this; schools, colleges, and universities have joined in; and numerous social and spiritual organizations are also involved. In just the last few days, thousands of pledge ceremonies and awareness programs have taken place across the country. Friends, there is one aspect of this campaign that I particularly appreciate: the ‘Nasha-Mukti Ka Sandesh.’ Our youth are propagating this message in their own language and in their own way.
I had urged young people in ‘Mann Ki Baat’ as well, to join this campaign using their creativity, and I am delighted that thousands of youth have stepped forward in response to this call. Various competitions - such as anthem - slogan writing, and street plays - have been organized on the ‘MY Bharat’ platform. Similarly, young people are sharing creative content on social media using the hashtag ‘#NashaMuktYuva’; in essence, the message, the medium, and the driving energy behind it all come from the youth themselves. In the coming days, activities such as health check-ups and meditation camps will also be conducted as part of this campaign.
Friends,
Several of our festivals are approaching soon. This time amidst the festive celebrations, let us also look around us. If any young person is drifting towards a harmful habit, talk to them. If someone is trying to break free from addiction, support them. Let us all work together to advance the resolve of a drug-free youth and a Viksit Bharat.
My dear countrymen,
I announced a talent hunt campaign for sports from the Red Fort this time. To ensure India continues to perform excellently, it is essential to reach out to villages and towns to discover sporting talent. At the same time, there are many individuals who have dedicated themselves to this very cause. Their sole passion is to discover talent and shape it.
In our Punjab, Rajinder Singh ji is doing exactly this work. Rajinder Singh ji is one such individual who also carries the title ‘Senior’ as part of his name. He was part of the team that won the gold medal in hockey at the 1980 Olympics. He shone at the 1982 World Cup. In 2001, India won the Men’s Junior World Cup title for the first time, whereas in 2003, the country clinched the Senior Asia Cup title. He played the role of the coach in both these tournaments. Now, he is pursuing his passion through the Round Glass Hockey Academy. Thanks to his efforts, new hockey astro-turfs are being laid in villages. Rajinder ji has a very clear focus: identifying children in villages that lack access to excellent coaching facilities. Through such initiatives, many players are securing spots at India's junior and senior levels. No matter how much Rajinder Singh ji’s dedication is lauded, it’s not enough.
My dear countrymen,
Amla, the Indian gooseberry is very familiar to all of us. Pickles and preserves i.e. murabba made from it are used in most households. Many people like Amla juice and Chyawanprash becomes an essential part of our daily routine during winter. Our elders have long spoken about the qualities of Amla across generations. Friends, this very Amla is now becoming a source of new possibilities in Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh. The bond between Pratapgarh and Amla is very old; farmers here have been growing it for generations.
Amla has given Pratapgarh a strong identity, and now, this long-standing identity is bringing new opportunities for local farmers and women. The 'One District One Product' (ODOP) has boosted local entrepreneurs involved in the Amla trade there. Today, around 100 units related to Amla processing are operational in Pratapgarh, with women connected with self-help groups playing a significant role. One such group is from Devgarh Kamasi village; women associated with the Savitri Phule Self-Help Group are producing Amla candy, preserves, and juice. Access to new markets through the ODOP scheme has also led to an increase in their income.
Similarly, there is a 'Vindhyavasini Self-Help Group' in a village. The women of this group are producing many such items like Amla pickle and digestive powder. These women received machinery for processing and access to loan facilities. They also got the opportunity to participate in local trade fairs, and in no time, their income saw a significant rise.
Friends,
Every region of our country certainly possesses some such unique specialty - be it a specific fruit, a traditional art form, or a unique skill. The 'One District, One Product' campaign aims to promote these very specialties.
Our endeavour should be to ensure that the identity of our villages and small towns is not confined merely to local markets; these products should reach other parts of the country and even global markets. This also strengthens the 'Vocal for Local' campaign… it inspires the nation to become self-reliant. Even during the upcoming festive season, we must never forget the 'Vocal for Local' mantra.
My dear countrymen,
The month of September is dedicated to the fight against malnutrition. During the Nutrition Month, individuals and organizations from various sectors come together for this noble cause.
Several commendable initiatives have been launched this year to combat malnutrition. Chhattisgarh, for instance, has started the 'Har Ghar Munga - Ghar Ghar Munga' campaign… through this, people are being encouraged to include the nutritious Munga i.e. Moringa in their diet. Gujarat has also launched a 'Vangi Spardha' - a competition featuring dishes made from millets. This initiative promotes affordable and nutritious local cuisine. So far, more than two lakh people have participated in this contest. Maharashtra is also making commendable efforts in this direction; teachers, Anganwadi workers, and parents are joining awareness campaigns there. In Mizoram as well, people have come together this year to launch a campaign for the upkeep of 'Poshan Vatikas'. This aligns with the Mizo tradition of 'Talo-Mad-Yana,' which signifies selfless service and always being at the forefront of helping others.
Such efforts are truly praiseworthy. I am also proud of everyone associated with Anganwadi centres who has been part of such initiatives. These Anganwadi centres are now digitally connected via the 'Poshan Tracker,' with approximately nine crore beneficiaries registered on the platform. This has enabled better care for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers. We must continue this fight against malnutrition with the same spirit; we have to make our society completely free from malnutrition.
Friends,
All of us have celebrated Ganesha Utsav this month with great devotion and enthusiasm. Ganpati Bappa was welcomed across the country with deep reverence. This sacred occasion fills the entire atmosphere with joy and exuberance. Friends, Vighnharta Bhagwan Shri Ganesha symbolizes knowledge, wisdom, and the auspicious beginning of any endeavour. Deep reverence for Him exists not only in India; take the example of Shriman Panthoun Thirkhanon ji - he hails from Thailand. There, Lord Shri Ganesha is worshipped as 'Phra Phikanet.' When he was 19 years old, his father gifted him a photograph of Bhagwan Shri Ganesha. It was then that a profound sense of devotion awakened within him. He has spent over four decades studying traditions associated with Bhagwan Shri Ganesha. He has travelled across several Asian countries, including India and Nepal. He has held a special affection for Maharashtra.
After learning about the Ashtavinayak tradition, he has visited the region numerous times. Through his efforts, the Ashtavinayak yatra has gained popularity among devotees in Thailand as well. In 2002, he established the Ganesha Himal Museum in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. Today, it houses more than 10,000 idols of Ganesha. The museum also has Ashtavinayak idols for devotees who are unable to travel to India. Worship rituals for Ganesha ji are conducted here every Sunday morning around 10 o'clock. Also, on special occasions connected with Ganesha, celebrations are held. This demonstrates how India's faith, art, and cultural traditions are gaining popularity in other countries as well. I wish that the blessings of Ganpati Bappa remain with everyone always.
Friends,
After every episode of ‘Mann Ki Baat,’ I receive messages from you on myriad topics. Do continue to share such inspiring stories. When you appreciate the initiatives taking place around you, the enthusiasm of those involved grows even further. Learning about these efforts through ‘Mann Ki Baat’ inspires people in other parts of the country as well. May this journey continue to move forward with your support. Celebrate the upcoming festivals with great joy and enthusiasm with your family and friends. I extend my best wishes to all of you once again.
Thank you very much.
Namaskar.

title: Two-Day National Conference on Rabi Campaign 2026 to Begin Tomorrow in New Delhi
subtitle:
Conference to Focus on Strengthening Centre–State Coordination and Evolving an Outcome-Oriented Strategy for Agriculture

State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 10:19AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Government of India, will organise the National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026 on 28–29 September 2026 at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi. The Conference will be inaugurated by Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and will bring together State Agriculture Ministers, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, ICAR and other stakeholders to deliberate on key priorities and preparedness for the forthcoming Rabi season.
The two-day Conference will focus on strengthening Centre–State coordination and evolving a coordinated, outcome-oriented strategy for enhancing agricultural production, productivity, sustainability and farmers’ incomes. The deliberations will also build upon the key learnings and outcomes of the recently held Zonal Conferences on Agriculture.
The first day will comprise three rounds of parallel thematic group discussions covering three broad areas: Atmanirbharta, Diversification and Production Growth; Sustainability and Climate-Resilient Agriculture; and Digital Agriculture, Infrastructure, Financing and Risk Management. Key issues to be deliberated upon will include the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, oilseeds and oil palm, horticulture, cotton, seed availability and reforms in the seed value chain, natural farming, soil health, farm mechanisation, FPO financing and infrastructure, marketing reforms, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, Kisan Credit Card coverage, Digital Agriculture, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, plant protection and agricultural statistics.
The thematic discussions are aimed at identifying key implementation challenges, State-specific priorities and actionable strategies for the Rabi season, with particular emphasis on improving convergence among schemes, strengthening delivery mechanisms and ensuring effective outcomes at the field level.
The second day will focus on the key learnings from the Zonal Conferences and outcomes of the thematic discussions held on the first day. The agenda will include the Rabi season weather outlook, fertilizer availability and balanced use of fertilizers, Digital Agriculture Mission, Farmer Registry, Digital Crop Survey and AgriStack, Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, National Mission on Edible Oils, crop and seed status, varietal adoption, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, marketing reforms and preparation of Agriculture Plans through ATMA and KVKs.
The Conference will also provide an opportunity for State Agriculture Ministers to share their views/experiences, state priorities and suggestions for agricultural development and Rabi season preparedness. The inputs from States, along with the outcomes of the thematic deliberations, are expected to contribute towards a coordinated and outcome-oriented strategy for the Rabi Campaign 2026.
The concluding session will focus on summarizing the deliberations and preparing a robust roadmap for enhancing the crop production of Rabi crops and empowering farmers to fulfil the vision of ‘Atmanirbharta & Viksit Bharat’ ensuring food & nutritional security.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Uttar Pradesh’s Growing Global Trade and Investment Opportunities
subtitle:
UP’s Entrepreneurs to Benefit from Expanding Global Market Access through Free Trade Agreements: Shri Goyal

Uttar Pradesh Targets Increase in Annual Exports from Around ₹2 Lakh Crore to ₹5 Lakh Crore by 2030: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 2:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted that as global markets open up to India through Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), Uttar Pradesh’s entrepreneurs will have greater opportunities to access international markets. Addressing the UP International Trade Show in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Goyal said that expanding exports, investments and global market access would contribute to the state’s goal of becoming a $1 trillion economy.
Shri Goyal said new investments are expected to flow into India from across the globe and noted that Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a preferred investment destination, supported by favourable industrial policies and proactive industrial schemes. He said major corporations and global investors are arriving across sectors, creating new employment opportunities.
The Minister highlighted the role of modern technology, international enterprises and the evolving craftsmanship and technical skills of Uttar Pradesh’s youth in driving the state’s development. He said international events of this scale provide opportunities for direct access to global markets, enabling Uttar Pradesh’s diverse products, cuisines and services to reach international markets.
Shri Goyal highlighted the international participation at the UP International Trade Show, including six partner countries, hundreds of delegates and exhibitors, and buyer-seller meetings. He noted the participation of international stakeholders and the opportunities created for businesses through the event.
The Minister highlighted the development of expressways, modern airports and industrial parks in Uttar Pradesh and noted the state’s growing presence across sectors including defence, semiconductors, electronics and other modern high-technology domains. He also referred to the expansion of a large robotics manufacturing facility in Greater Noida as an example of modern industrial growth and technological development.
Shri Goyal said the next frontier for Uttar Pradesh’s development lies in expanding exports in global markets, attracting international investments, strengthening tourism and building global recognition for brands from the state. He said Uttar Pradesh is strengthening its foundation for greater global trade and progressing towards its development objectives.
The Minister noted that Uttar Pradesh currently has an annual export volume of around ₹2 lakh crore and has set a target to increase this to ₹5 lakh crore by 2030.
Shri Goyal said the expanding global market access through FTAs, investments, tourism and international recognition of Uttar Pradesh’s products and brands would create new opportunities for the state’s entrepreneurs. He called for active participation and cooperation from the state’s trade and industrial community in taking forward this development journey.
The Minister also highlighted the importance of coordination between the central and state Governments, along with the participation of citizens, youth and stakeholders from the trade and industrial sector, in supporting Uttar Pradesh’s continued economic and export growth.

title: Rajasthan’s Art, Faith, Royalty and Sporting Legacy on Display at PM Mementos e-Auction 2026
subtitle: The collection brings together folk deities, traditional art, textiles, heritage sites and sporting memorabilia, offering a glimpse into Rajasthan’s diverse traditions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Rajasthan’s rich tapestry of art, devotion, craftsmanship and tradition comes alive in a diverse collection of mementos featured in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026. The collection brings together 37 artefacts representing the state’s folk deities, traditional paintings, textiles, architectural heritage and sporting achievements.
Among the prominent pieces is a handcrafted Ambabari elephant with Howdah, carved from wood and decorated with traditional patterns. Another handcrafted wooden elephant procession set depicts a royal howdah accompanied by ceremonial attendants.
The collection highlights a silver memento of Veer Tejaji Maharaj depicts the revered folk deity mounted on a horse, while another silver-plated statue portrays him riding his horse with his characteristic spear and snake motif.
The collection includes Pichwai paintings of Shrinathji from Nathdwara, a Phad painting depicting Lakshmi and Narayan and a Pattachitra-style artwork portraying Krishna Raas Leela. These works showcase different forms of devotional storytelling and artistic expression represented in the catalogue.
The cultural diversity of the collection extends to Ajmer Sharif Dargah, represented through both a hand-painted artwork and a framed depiction of the shrine. The catalogue describes the painting as capturing the architectural character of the Dargah and its tradition of welcoming devotees from different faiths.
A decorated turban featuring a stone and feather brooch, a yellow pagdi with multicoloured motifs, and several angavastras featuring gota borders showcase the region’s textile and ornamental traditions.
The collection further features representations of several revered sites and deities, including Kaila Mata of Karauli, Sundha Mata, Khema Baba of Baytu, Brahma Temple in Pushkar and Shri Kalyan Raiji Maharaj. A painting of Mangarh Dham in Banswara also forms part of the collection.
Alongside these cultural and sporting artefacts are historical and contemporary memorabilia, including framed newspaper editions related to the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha and a decorative plate artwork issued by BJP Rajasthan.
Together, the 37 mementos present a varied portrait of Rajasthan through its folk traditions, devotional art, painting, textiles, historical heritage, architecture and contemporary achievements, bringing several facets of the state’s cultural identity into the PM Mementos e-Auction.
The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, live until 2 October 2026, brings together mementos representing Rajasthan’s rich cultural heritage and traditions. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal:
pmmementos.gov.in

title: EXERCISE TARANG SHAKTI 2026: “POWER IN PARTNERSHIP”
subtitle: IAF COMMENCES OPERATIONAL PHASE AT JODHPUR
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Following the inaugural ceremony held yesterday, the Indian Air Force (IAF) is set to commence the operational phase of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur. Being conducted from 26 September to 12 October 2026, the multilateral air exercise is themed “Power in Partnership”, underscoring the strength that comes from working together, sharing expertise and building interoperability among partner air forces.
Seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) — Australia, the United States of America, the United Arab Emirates, France, Germany, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh — are participating in the exercise. The foreign aircraft taking part include the F-35 Lightning II, Rafale, F-16, A400M, MRTT, C-130, C-130J and KC-30A, bringing together a diverse mix of combat, airlift and air-to-air refuelling capabilities.
Building on the successful inaugural edition in 2024, Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 provides participating air forces an opportunity for advanced joint training, exchange of operational expertise and consolidation of professional experience. The participating contingents will operate alongside the IAF, employing frontline combat platforms and support elements across a range of missions. Several other FFCs will also participate as observers.
The exercise will facilitate professional interaction among aircrew, mission planners and operational support personnel, with emphasis on interoperability, mutual learning, aerospace safety and enhanced understanding of operational procedures. The interaction will provide participating forces an opportunity to operate together, share experiences and gain a better understanding of each other's capabilities and operating philosophies.
This edition of Tarang Shakti has a wider canvas beyond flying operations, with a range of professional, cultural and outreach activities planned during the exercise. These include a dedicated seminar, industrial tour for the participating foreign contingents, Sekhon Marathon, heritage tours and yoga sessions. These engagements will provide opportunities for professional exchange, exposure to India's aerospace and industrial ecosystem, and greater interaction and camaraderie among the participating contingents.
Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 provides the IAF an opportunity to demonstrate its operational capabilities, professional standards and institutional ethos, while highlighting India's growing indigenous aerospace and defence capabilities. The exercise, under the theme “Power in Partnership”, reinforces the importance of cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust in building enduring partnerships among participating air forces.
The exercise reaffirms India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and enhanced military cooperation in support of regional peace, security and stability, while strengthening partnerships and fostering greater strategic cooperation through shared operational experience.

title: India Does Not Seek to Occupy Any Country’s Territory, But Will Safeguard Its Security and Strategic Autonomy When Threatened: Rajnath Singh
subtitle:
As a Civilizational Power, India’s Rise is in the Interest of the Entire World

India Moving from Defence Importer to Trusted Global Defence Supplier

National Unity is Essential for National Security: Rajnath Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 SEP 2026 1:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“India believes in peace and does not seek to occupy the territory of any country. However, peace should not be mistaken for weakness. We seek global stability, but not at the cost of our strategic autonomy. We are firmly committed to safeguarding our security and strategic autonomy when threatened,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing a Defence Conclave in New Delhi on September 27, 2026.
Raksha Mantri underlined that there can be no scope for dialogue with any country that promotes terrorism against India. “Countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy or provide shelter and support to terrorists must be firmly reminded that terrorism cannot be a strategic asset for any nation. He asserted that as long as a neighbouring country continues to pursue a policy of supporting terrorism, India remains fully entitled to take all necessary measures against terrorism”, he said, referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s remarks at the recent SCO meeting.
Emphasising national unity as a key pillar of national security, the Raksha Mantri stated that the security of the country is not solely the responsibility of the armed forces but a collective responsibility of every citizen. He urged citizens to rise above divisions based on religion, caste, creed, language, region and other identities, and to place national interest above personal and narrow interests.
Shri Rajnath Singh described India as a civilizational power whose rise is based on inclusive development rather than confrontation or disruption. He outlined three foundations of India’s approach: its long democratic and civilizational traditions, the principle of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ and the vision of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, and five strategic pillars—respect, dialogue, prosperity, security and culture.
Focusing on the Global South, Raksha Mantri highlighted India’s growing role as a trusted partner and ‘Vishwa Bandhu’. He noted that under Vaccine Maitri, India supplied more than 30 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses to over 100 countries and has supported developing nations through medicines, digital payment solutions, expertise and resources. He also highlighted initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summits to advance the interests of developing countries. Emphasising responsible use of power, he called for cooperation even amid competition and inclusive participation in global development.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted India’s significant progress towards self-reliance in defence, noting that the country is developing indigenous capabilities ranging from aircraft and drone engines to fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets. India’s defence exports have grown from just ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to a record ₹38,424 crore in 2025–26, reaching more than 100 countries. After achieving the ₹30,000-crore export target last year, India has now set a target of ₹50,000 crore by 2029.
He emphasised that growing international demand for Indian missiles, radars, ammunition and defence platforms reflects global confidence in India’s technology, quality and delivery capabilities. Consequently, “Made in India” is increasingly emerging not merely as a manufacturing label, but as a symbol of trust in Indian defence capabilities.
Raksha Mantri highlighted the significant increase in defence allocation, which has reached ₹7.85 lakh crore in 2026-27, compared to around ₹2.53 lakh crore in 2013-14. He noted that around 75% of the capital acquisition budget, amounting to ₹1.39 lakh crore, has been earmarked for procurement from the domestic defence industry, thereby strengthening indigenous manufacturing and associated MSME supply chains.
Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the nature of warfare is rapidly changing, with modern conflicts extending beyond conventional domains to cyber, space, electronic and information warfare, alongside emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, drones, autonomous systems, quantum technology and hypersonic systems. He underlined the need for India to develop future-ready capabilities across these domains.
Highlighting India’s efforts to address strategic vulnerabilities in areas such as technology, energy, data and supply chains, the Raksha Mantri said that initiatives are underway to strengthen domestic capabilities in semiconductors and critical minerals, diversify energy sources and enhance energy security.
Emphasising the importance of self-reliance, the Raksha Mantri stated that 509 defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms have been included in five positive indigenisation lists issued by the Armed Forces. DPSUs have also released six indigenisation lists covering 5,417 items, including strategically important LRUs, subsystems, spares and components, of which around 3,300 have been indigenised.
He highlighted the growing participation of the private sector, startups and MSMEs in defence manufacturing. India’s defence ecosystem now includes DPSUs, private industries, more than 16,000 MSMEs, startups, universities and research institutions, with defence manufacturing capabilities emerging across several regions of the country. Investment proposals of about ₹70,000 crore have been received in the Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridors, with around ₹10,000 crore already invested.
Raksha Mantri also highlighted the role of the SRIJAN and SRIJAN DEEP portals in strengthening indigenous defence supply chains. He stated that around 33,000 imported items have been identified for import substitution through SRIJAN, of which approximately 15,700 have been indigenised. SRIJAN DEEP has created a national digital database covering more than 40,000 manufacturers and sellers and lakhs of products.
Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the transformation of the DPSU and Ordnance Factory ecosystem, noting that corporatisation of the Ordnance Factories has enhanced their technology orientation, output and accountability. He stated that all 16 DPSUs are currently operating without losses and are increasing their focus on research, development and exports.
Highlighting the role of youth and innovation, he said that iDEX and iDEX-Prime are providing opportunities for startups and innovators to contribute to national security, while programmes such as ADITI are supporting advanced defence technologies. As of March 2026, 676 startups and innovators had been engaged through iDEX and 551 contracts signed. The Ministry has also approved procurement worth more than ₹2,400 crore from startups/MSMEs and development projects worth over ₹1,500 crore.
A significant announcement was the decision to transfer DRDO-developed technologies for conventional missile systems to eligible Indian industries, enabling qualifying private companies to undertake production. Shri Rajnath Singh said the move would strengthen the preparedness of the Armed Forces and facilitate timely delivery of missiles. He added that DRDO is increasingly being positioned to focus on research and development while industry assumes a greater role in production.
Raksha Mantri concluded that India’s objective is to build indigenous capabilities across the entire defence spectrum—from individual components to complete weapon systems—and to develop technologies domestically rather than remain dependent on imports. He stressed that this approach is aimed at strengthening strategic autonomy, defence preparedness and a resilient indigenous defence-industrial ecosystem.

content:
The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, organised the fourth edition of the ‘Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk @ NZP’, including the second walk held during the Big Butterfly Month, and the fifteenth edition of the ‘Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP’ as part of its ongoing efforts to promote citizen participation in biodiversity monitoring, species documentation and wildlife conservation awareness. The walks were conducted from 6:30 AM to 10:30 AM under the expert guidance of Sh. Rohit Sharma, Bird Expert, and Sh. Ramver, Butterfly and Dragonfly Expert, along with dedicated volunteers.
The programme received an enthusiastic response from bird and butterfly enthusiasts, nature lovers, students, wildlife photographers and citizens interested in biodiversity conservation. A total of 15 participants took part in the walks. The event was attended by the Director, National Zoological Park, zoo officials and resource experts, who guided and interacted with the participants throughout the activity.
During the walks, participants documented 47 bird species, with observations of more than 750 individual birds, along with 8 butterfly species, 10 dragonfly species and 5 damselfly species in the walk area. The observations provided valuable field-level information and encouraged participants to actively contribute to biodiversity documentation. The observations highlighted the rich diversity of butterflies and odonates within the National Zoological Park and reinforced the importance of regular field-based biodiversity documentation.
The experts shared valuable insights into the ecology, behaviour and conservation of birds, butterflies and dragonflies, highlighting their important ecological roles as pollinators, natural pest controllers and indicators of ecosystem health. The programme also provided participants with an opportunity to connect with nature, strengthen their species-identification skills and develop a deeper appreciation of biodiversity and wildlife conservation.
Addressing the participants, Dr. Sanjeet Kumar, Director, National Zoological Park, highlighted that such nature walks provide valuable opportunities to strengthen field-identification skills, improve understanding of food webs, contribute to biodiversity documentation and foster a deeper appreciation of wildlife and biodiversity conservation. The programme concluded with an interactive discussion, a participant feedback session and a group photograph with the experts and zoo officials.
Participation in each Sunday Nature Walk is limited to 20–25 participants to ensure a meaningful and high-quality learning experience. Prior registration is mandatory and is accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Interested participants may register through the designated Google Form, which remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The registration link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, and through the ‘NZP Sathi’ mobile application.
Further, the NZP New Delhi, would be celebrating the Wildlife Week 2026 from 2nd October to 8th October 2026. A wide range of educational, awareness and participatory activities will be organised during the week to promote wildlife conservation and encourage greater public participation.
The activities planned during Wildlife Week include: Tree Walk, Birds Walk, Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk, Spider and Insect Walk, Reptile, Amphibian and Molluscs Walk, Keeper’s Talk and Enclosure Enrichment, Clay Modeling Competition, Wildlife Poster Making  Competition, Debate Competition, Essay Writing Competition, Bird Nest Making competition, Bird Feeder Making competition, Leaf Craft competition, Drawing Competition, Treasure hunt Activity, Rangoli Competition, Quiz Competition, Expert Talk,  and Online Photography competition, Online Wildlife Poster Making  Competition & online Quiz Activity will be conducted from 02.10.2026 to
08.10.2026.
Detailed information regarding the competitions and other programmes will be made available on the official website of the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, and through the NZP Sathi mobile application. On the occasion of Wildlife Week, the National Zoological Park has invited school students from government and private schools across Delhi-NCR to participate in the various offline and online activities and competitions.
No fee will be charged for any Wildlife Week activity, walk or competition. Free entry to the National Zoological Park will be provided to all participants of Wildlife Week activities and competitions, along with their school teachers, accompanying staff and parents, from 2nd October to 8th October 2026. In addition, children up to 12 years of age will be provided free entry to the National Zoological Park during these dates as part of the Wildlife Week celebrations. Through these initiatives, the NZP seeks to strengthen public engagement with nature, promote citizen science and biodiversity documentation, and foster greater awareness and participation in wildlife conservation.

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the inaugural ceremony of the centenary year celebrations organised in New Delhi to commemorate the birth anniversary of former President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Ashok Singhal. Several dignitaries were present on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that it is a matter of pride for all of us to be present here for the inauguration of the centenary celebrations of the revered Ashok Ji. He said that Ashok Ji was born a hundred years ago and remained exemplary at every stage of his life. As a student, he excelled; as a Swayamsevak, he excelled; and as a Pracharak, he continued to distinguish himself. When he was entrusted with the responsibility of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, he continued to lead a life devoted to Hindutva with unwavering dedication until his last breath and succeeded in his mission. Such personalities are rarely seen. Shri Shah said that simplicity, exemplary patriotism, devotion to Dharma, commitment to the Swayamsevak ideal and a spirit of struggle—all these qualities were embodied together in Ashok Ji’s life. He was born into a highly prestigious and affluent family. Despite being born into such a family, he remained steadfastly simple in his way of life, the result of which is before us today. He said that we have witnessed the construction of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple, for which the entire Hindu society had been making sacrifices, struggling and coming together for the moment that had been awaited for five and a half centuries. He said that the room at the VHP, where Ashok Ji spent twenty years of his life, has today become almost like an exhibition space for workers. To live with such simplicity and uphold such exemplary patriotism is truly rare.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that even at an advanced age, Ashok Ji would work for sixteen hours a day. His sole source of inspiration was exemplary patriotism. Ashok Ji held immense respect for Hindu Dharma, the Vedas, the Upanishads, Sanskrit, Indian culture and the tradition of saints. Throughout his life, he maintained a deep sense of reverence for all these. He believed that if anyone or anything could contribute to the welfare of the entire universe, it was Hindu Dharma, the Vedas and the Upanishads. Citing the Shanti Mantra as an example, he explained that the objective of enhancing the stature of Hindu Dharma and establishing it in the world was not because we are Hindus, but because Hindu Dharma envisions the welfare of the entire universe. He had said that Guru Golwalkar Ji’s words were that the foundation of our work could only be selfless and pure love, and nothing else. Such an exalted personality remained a Swayamsevak throughout his life. Ashok Ji faithfully followed every discipline of the life of a Pracharak, without seeking glorification or publicity.
Shri Amit Shah said that when it comes to struggle, Ashok Ji is known to everyone for his spirit of struggle. The Ram Janmabhoomi movement was deeply embedded in his heart and mind. He firmly believed that India could attain a position of glory and prestige in the world only by removing the stigma of slavery and constructing a grand Ram Temple. He devoted his entire life to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Shri Shah said that when the then Government of Uttar Pradesh ordered a brutal lathi charge, Ashok Ji reached the frontline in disguise. He was also injured in the lathi charge. He said that the image of Ashok Ji wiping blood from his face with a gamchha should remain etched in the memory of the youth for a hundred years. What true dedication means is evident from Ashok Ji’s life and deeds.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the Vishwa Hindu Parishad, the institution of saints, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, the construction of the temple and the Sangh were among the subjects closest to Ashok Ji’s heart. He always spoke openly about these causes and worked to advance them. All these institutions and causes became synonymous with his identity. He himself was an institution. Ashok Ji’s life is an institution in itself for many adolescents and young people. He expressed confidence that the celebration of Ashok Ji’s birth centenary would make him a source of inspiration for many young people and adolescents throughout their lives. The essence of his life, his penance, his simplicity and his dedication and endeavour are qualities worthy of emulation by every young person. The remembrance of his life will naturally continue to awaken and inspire the youth.
Shri Amit Shah said that there was no distinction between Ashok Ji’s personal and public life. He had imbibed the ideal of living for the nation and merged his personal life completely with this principle. He accepted organisational work as a form of spiritual practice. He said that merely remembering Ashok Ji’s name is not the purpose of the programme. The centenary year is an endeavour to take his qualities to every household, particularly to the youth. Some people ask why there is a need to celebrate the birth centenary of someone who never sought publicity. I would humbly say that gratitude is not merely a sentiment; it is a national necessity. The birth centenary is necessary so that the entire country and Hindus across the world can express their gratitude to Ashok Ji. When a nation and society do not remember their heroes and fail to take their lives and teachings to the youth, an ideological vacuum emerges. There are no ideals to look up to, no direction to follow and no source of inspiration. People then begin looking for ideals in civilisations thousands of kilometres away. Therefore, it is essential to ensure that an ideological vacuum does not arise in society, that worthy ideals are placed before the people, and that the life of Ashok Ji provides direction and inspiration. This is why celebrating his birth centenary is extremely important.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today we witnessed presentations of various service initiatives that embody the essence of Hindutva, including prayers at the temples of Sant Ravidas Ji and Maharishi Valmiki Ji, the Ganga Aarti in Prayagraj, Ganga conservation, service to Gaumata, the commemoration of the Ram Setu movement, and the donation of artificial limbs in Ayodhya. The digital inauguration of 11 Shri Ram Stambhs was also held. These pillars commemorate the route taken by Maryada Purushottam Shri Ram during his exile. Without uttering a word, these pillars will convey to generations to come the message of the Ram Van Gaman Path and the virtues of Shri Ram.
Shri Amit Shah said that there is a sense of regret that Ashok Ji, who had dedicated himself to the struggle for the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, could not witness the Bhoomi Pujan or see the temple completed. However, he never worked with the objective of witnessing the fulfilment of his efforts in his own lifetime. He would always say that this was a struggle spanning generations. He said that countless people would fight, several generations would pass, and only then would victory be achieved. He said that wherever Ashok Ji’s soul may be, it must be experiencing that the transformation that came about in the country in 2014 changed the direction of governance. After Prime Minister Modi came to office, the governmental obstacles were removed within just five years, and the grand temple of Prabhu Shri Ram was constructed without bloodshed. He said that this is not only a matter of peace and satisfaction for the country, but also for all devotees of Shri Ram across the world.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that he shares Ashok Ji’s faith that the construction of the Ram Temple would open a new path for India’s progress. He said that our ideas, our culture, our Dharma and its virtues would reach people across the world. He said that Ashok Ji believed that one should remain committed to Hindutva because the welfare of the entire universe is possible only on the basis of the ideals of Hindutva. He expressed the hope that the youth of the country would continue to draw values and inspiration from Ashok Ji’s personality, life, contributions and words for generations to come.

date:

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated development projects worth ₹1,472 crore and flagged off the country’s first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati Railway Station in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. He also inaugurated the WAG-12 Maintenance Shed being established for the maintenance of railway locomotive engines. Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.
Addressing the programme, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that several railway projects have been initiated today in the Sabarmati division, focusing on environmental sustainability, passenger amenities and the safety of rail passengers. He said, Satyagraha, simple living, rural development and khadi, the journey of translating all these experiments into action on the ground began from Sabarmati itself. Shri Amit Shah said that Sabarmati Railway Station has now undergone significant development, but in the 1980s, passengers had to walk nearly two kilometres even to find a rickshaw from the station. He said that the Sabarmati Railway Station has witnessed a major transformation in terms of passenger amenities, safety and connectivity. Shri Shah said that the development works inaugurated and foundation stones laid today, at a cost of ₹1,472 crore, will prove to be highly significant for the region in the coming days. He said that a WAG-12 Maintenance Shed has been constructed here at a cost of ₹700 crore for the maintenance of railway locomotive engines. The ‘Kavach’ train protection system has been introduced on the Sabarmati–Kalol–Sabarmati rail section at a cost of ₹48 crore to enhance safety. In addition, works have commenced for the implementation of ‘Kavach’ on the Ahmedabad–Palanpur and Ahmedabad–Samakhiali rail sections, as well as the doubling of the Sabarmati–Sarkhej railway line.
Shri Amit Shah said that today, an engine with a 12,000-horsepower twin-section capacity has been commissioned, which can haul nearly as much freight as 600 trucks single-handedly. Earlier, two locomotives were required for this purpose, but now a single WAG-12 can perform the same task. He said that this will mark an important milestone in the history of Indian Railways. Shri Shah said that a LNG-powered train has also been inaugurated today, which will make a significant contribution to environmental conservation in the years to come.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that after Shri Narendra Modi became Prime Minister in 2014, several new facilities were introduced in the railways and the railway network was modernised. He said that the successful trial of the country’s first double-stack long-haul container train from Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT), Mumbai, to Vadodara has been completed. He said that the country has limited rail tracks for freight transportation, but if the concept of double-stack freight trains succeeds, the freight-carrying capacity will nearly double. He said that an 11,000-kilometre-long corridor is now being converted into a four-lane network, which will significantly facilitate traffic movement towards Delhi–Howrah and Delhi–Guwahati.
Shri Amit Shah said that it was under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi that the Dedicated Freight Corridors, the Rapid Rail System and premium railway stations were introduced. He said that recently, Prime Minister Modi inaugurated a hydrogen-powered train, making India one of only four countries in the world to possess this technology. He said that 97 per cent of bio-toilets were installed during the Modi government’s tenure. 87 per cent of LHB coaches were manufactured in India during the Modi government’s tenure. Railway electrification stood at only 30 per cent before Prime Minister Modi assumed office, while the remaining 70 per cent was completed during his tenure. He said that under the Modi government, the railway safety budget has increased by 67 per cent, while locomotive production capacity has increased by 66 per cent.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Modi launched the concepts of ‘Make in India’ and ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’, and as a result, the country has now made significant progress towards manufacturing equipment such as locomotives domestically. He said that in 2015–16, the railways consumed 293 crore litres of diesel, but this has declined to 108 crore litres in 2024–25. He said this is a major achievement that receives relatively little attention. Shri Shah said that railway electrification was only 75 kilometres in an entire year in 2010–11, whereas 7,188 kilometres were electrified in a single year in 2023–24. He said that 99.6 per cent of the railway network has now been electrified, and the remaining 0.4 per cent will also be completed soon. He said that railway electrification stands at 92 per cent in China, 68 per cent in Spain, 60 per cent in France and 49 per cent in the United Kingdom, a relatively small country. India will surpass these countries by achieving 100 per cent electrification. He said that Sweden is the only country in the world to have achieved 100 per cent railway electrification, but the total length of railway lines in Sweden is nearly ten times less than that of India.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that, if Gujarat is taken as an example in terms of the railway budget, the rail budget from 2009 to 2014 was merely ₹589 crore. In contrast, the budget for just one year, 2026–27, stands at ₹17,366 crore. He said that the difference in the pace of development is clearly visible. He said that the people of the country should tell opposition party leaders who make reckless statements to discuss issues with facts and figures. Shri Shah questioned the opposition party about what it had done during its tenure. He said that apart from scams, scandals and corruption amounting to ₹12 lakh crore over 10 years, the opposition party had done nothing. Shri Shah said that in 12 years, not even the slightest allegation of corruption has been levelled against Modi Ji.

Speaking at the inaugural function of the World Congress on Nanomedicine 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh described nanomedicine as one of the most transformative developments in medical practice, with the potential to make healthcare increasingly precise and personalised by working at the nanometre scale. Nobel Laureate Prof. Roger D. Kornberg, Nobel Laureate and Stanford University, USA, is the Chairperson of the Congress, while Prof. T.M.S. Chang, McGill University, Canada, is the Honorary President. Prof. Yogesh Singh, Vice-Chancellor, University of Delhi; Prof. G.P. Talwar; Prof. Gobardhan Das, Member, NITI Aayog; Prof. Ramesh Chandra; and Prof. Indrajit Roy were among the distinguished participants present at the inaugural session.
Dr. Jitendra Singh explained that nanomedicine involves the application of nanotechnology in medicine, working with structures at the scale of one-billionth of a metre. He said that as medicine moves towards precision healthcare, patients suffering from the same disease may increasingly require different treatment approaches depending on their genetic profile, lifestyle, dietary habits and environmental factors. Nanotechnology, by enabling interventions at the cellular level, can play an important role in making such treatment more precise.
The Minister said nanomedicine will also have significance beyond healthcare, with its applications expected to influence the cost-effectiveness of health processes and contribute to the wider economy. He referred to the growing global interest in nanomedicine as an indication of the scale of opportunity emerging in this field.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also cautioned against excessive dependence on technology in medical practice. He said that while technologies such as Artificial Intelligence and nanotechnology are opening new possibilities, they must complement the clinical sense of doctors rather than compromise it. The challenge, he said, is to synergise advanced technology with the human and clinical dimensions of medicine.
Calling for reinventing medical teaching in response to rapid technological changes, Dr. Jitendra Singh recalled that medical education traditionally placed strong emphasis on diagnosing patients through careful observation and physical examination. He said these foundational clinical skills should continue to remain relevant even as technological tools become increasingly sophisticated.
Giving details of the Government’s support for nanomedicine research, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Department of Biotechnology is supporting 210 R&D projects in nanomedicine with financial support of ₹174 crore. The projects cover targeted drug delivery, cancer nanomedicine, infectious-disease nanomedicine, nucleic-acid and vaccine delivery, nano-diagnostics and imaging, regenerative medicine and wound healing, as well as nanotoxicology and regulatory science.
Among the promising research areas, the Minister referred to oral insulin nanoparticles and nanobots for breast cancer, besides precision nanoinjection and targeted breast cancer nanomedicine. He recalled that earlier efforts towards oral insulin faced challenges related to absorption and digestive enzymes, and said advances in nanotechnology could provide new possibilities for addressing such challenges.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s nanomedicine ecosystem is expanding beyond laboratory research, with government support extending to StartUps, infrastructure, technology development and regulatory facilitation. Through BIRAC, emerging biotechnology enterprises can access support through programmes including Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG), Promoting Academic Research Conversion to Enterprise (PACE), Small Business Innovation Research Initiative (SBIRI) and Biotechnology Industry Partnership Programme (BIPP), helping translate research into enterprise and products.
He further said India has established a regulatory framework for nanopharmaceuticals through guidelines jointly developed by DBT, ICMR and CDSCO, providing a framework for evaluating the safety, quality and efficacy of nanopharmaceutical products.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is already into this relatively new area of medicine and has the scientific and institutional capabilities to contribute to the development of future healthcare solutions. He said the country’s expanding research base, government support and growing industry engagement provide a foundation for India to move from adoption of emerging technologies towards developing solutions of its own.
Prof. Roger D. Kornberg, Nobel Laureate and Stanford University, described nanomedicine as a young and rapidly evolving field with significant potential for the future of healthcare. He said nanomedicine offers the promise of precision, delivering the right amount of treatment to the right place at the right time, while improving effectiveness and reducing toxicity, with applications spanning drug delivery, diagnosis, imaging and regenerative medicine.
The World Congress on Nanomedicine 2026 is being organised under the umbrella of the International Society of Nano Medical Sciences (ISNS) and International Society for Nano Medicine (ISNM) and provides a platform for scientists, researchers, students and industry to exchange knowledge, build collaborations and engage with emerging developments in nanomedicine.
